headlines.title: Welcome to the New Era of Bond Yields at 5%
headlines.summary: The long bond cracking 5% isn't a headline — it's a regime change. When Treasuries start competing with equities on yield, every discount rate model on the Street gets repriced, and the tape feels it from small caps to REITs to growth tech. This is the single biggest macro force in the room right now, and the 30-year mortgage jumping to 7.45% tells you the pain is already bleeding into the real economy.

headlines.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz within 7 days and restart nuclear talks
headlines.summary: If Hormuz reopens, you're looking at an immediate bid-side collapse in crude — and that's the one variable that's been torching bond markets, equity multiples, and airline stocks simultaneously. A phased deal here is the single biggest potential relief valve for global inflation expectations, which means it touches everything from the Fed's next move to energy sector positioning. Don't get too excited yet — the Houthis are still lobbing missiles at Riyadh as we speak.

headlines.title: Warsh's regime change at the Fed pushes ahead – and meets resistance
headlines.summary: A new Fed chair driving rapid structural change while keeping further rate hikes on the table is not background noise — that's the bid under volatility for the foreseeable future. Markets have been trying to price in Warsh's framework all week, and the uncertainty premium is showing up in the long end of the curve. Every rate-sensitive sector from housing to financials to utilities is watching this one closely.
